quotes.excerpt: The Dirt Beneath the Devil #1 is an amazing opening issue for the series that will surely trap readers’ interest in reading more of the series. The mysteries that this issue either straight out tells us or implies are enough to peek even the most jaded readers’ interest. The premise that is laid out here in the first issue is intriguing, but when you know that Panosian obviously has more in store for us that jacks the intrigued levels all the way up. This should be a slam dunk pick up at the shop or Neon Ichiban this week. As a matter of fact, make sure to add this one to your Pull List as you won’t want to miss a single issue of this series.
The Dirt Beneath the Devil #1 is a solid debut issue. It takes a familiar concept and puts it in a setting that feels rather new and fresh.

The Big Shakedown #1 is a confident debut that pairs imaginative post-disaster worldbuilding with a compelling lead and a strong central mystery. Jordan Blum and Tim Seeley establish a fractured California that feels dangerous, satirical, and lived in, while Scott Koblish and Hi-Fi give the setting vivid visual character. With Ester’s personal goals tied directly to the missing-person case, the issue delivers an engaging start and plenty of reasons to return. This should be a strong contender when deciding what to pick up at the shop this week. Trust me once you read this first issue you will definitely want to add this series to your Pull List.

The Big Shakedown‘s premiere issue is a gritty post-natural disaster mystery with more unanswered questions and mystery than those answered. Tim Seeley. Jordan Blum, and Scott Koblish deliver a fresh tale with an edge and mystery that pulls you into a dark and frightening Los Angeles that is even hard for the reader to escape. The Big Shakedown is a vivid, character-driven mystery that turns a shattered Los Angeles into an intriguing and frightening noir setting.
Overall fun, compelling and pretty to look at, another great issue from the Sonic creative team and I look forward to seeing how this mini-arc wraps up.

Chachu #2 is a stellar follow up to the premier issue. Vellani continues to show that she has knack for storytelling and the art team continues to stun. The art, the setting, the coming of age story, I love everything about this series so far.

It don't feel like it's hitting a page just the right way. There's a kind of calm sophistication about the way Tyrone package is being presented on the page. Advanced motion and motion, poison posture fill the page in the way that feels very distinct. And very much unlike just about anything else on the comic rack today. No fantasy. No science fiction. Even the crime seems to be somewhere in the background it gets deeply into a very easy earthbound look at the way people interact who are our families who might be strangers. A very sharp, look at the way people connect.

The things that Haun and his team are doing are truly electric and terrifying. “Dooney Hollow” is for those that love slow burn horror with plenty of mystery and fall vibes. If you want that, then you need to pick this up!

The Folk of Dooney Hollow #1 is a compelling horror debut that pairs a steadily unfolding mystery with atmospheric artwork and an unsettling Ozark setting. Its strong pacing, memorable final reveal, and lingering unanswered questions make the next issue an easy recommendation. Make sure to pick a copy of this first issue up when you are at the shop this week. Also, well you are there, you should just add this to your Pull List as I’m confident that you will want more of this amazing and eerie world.
Power Rangers: Green #1 delivers a unique take on the post-apocalyptic story, and a new version of Tommy Oliver.

This debut issue brings back an iconic original Ranger in a futuristic setting. No longer a practicing Ranger, but the last Ranger in existence. Teaming up with an old foe to take on a new threat that is bringing Tommy out of retirement. This issue doesn’t answer some of the more pivotal questions surrounding Tommy, but it paints a comforting picture that he is living a more simplistic life. This is a must-read for Power Ranger fans! So make sure you pick up your copy of this new miniseries and add this to your “pull list.”A little bonus for this review! I had the opportunity to speak with Pallie Paul Allor about this issue as well as what readers can expect in issue two. If you are a fan of Alpha, you are going to want to see what he does in this debut issue because it leads to much more from him physically in issue two!
Ryan North continues to craft a legendary Fantastic Four run. Each issue is so different yet they all work. The stories are unique, refreshing, and enjoyable
All in all, a fun journey through space and its consequences for the Fantastic Four. A good classic-style story before the DNX crossover begins!
Bleeding Hearts #7 continues to prove that its greatest strength is its characters, delivering another emotionally rich chapter that makes the wait for the next issue even harder.

Bleeding Hearts #7 kicks off the second story arc with a laugh, and by the end will have you on the verge of tears.  Deniz Camp and Stipan Morian have put together a book that defies expectation with each issue—one where, just like Poke himself, there is a real beating heart beneath all its undead exterior.  If you passed on this book because you were "all zombied out," pick up issue #7 and give it a shot.  I wouldn't be surprised if you find yourself going back to pick up the first six.
G.I. Joe #25 is a major milestone done right, paying off years of buildup and kicking off the series' most epic storyline yet.

G.I. JOE #25 is a phenomenal start to the Nightforce story arc. Joshua Williamson, Tom Reilly and Andrea Milana pace things out that you feel like you are experiencing the start of a big blockbuster event. Everything that happens in this issue comes across as being a payoff for many sub-plots that have been developed since the start of the series. Where the payoff leads to is anyone’s guess, leaving you as the reader even more excited to find out what happens next.

Superman #40 is damn near perfect. This arc acted as a bit of a redemption for Superboy Prime and I absolutely adore him after this. Whilst the story here is wrapped up, this isn’t the last time we will see Superboy Prime and there seems to be a bright future ahead for him and his “supporting characters”.

This has been a phenomenal story setting up Prime’s future, but special credit once again goes to Dan Mora, who plays with the nature of the comic book format in some incredibly unique ways. The original Superman is back next month for the kickoff of the big “Kingdom of Zod” event, but I hope Williamson gets to keep writing Prime for a long time.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #300 (#20) not only pushes the great story that we have been following forward, but also gives this milestone issue a big feel as well. The drama, action, surprises, and emotions are firing on all cylinders in this issue. If this issue doesn’t make you feel something you may need to check your pulse. They could’ve just phoned this one in as the 300th issue milestone is more than enough to sell the book. But they didn’t phone it in at all and crafted an issue that is sure to bring readers back next month for issue 21. If Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles is not on your Pull List already it needs to be added ASAP! If you are a comic book collector this 300th issue needs to be added to your collection as well. Cheers to 300 issues of TMNT and can’t wait for the 400th milestone issue!

This issue takes you on an emotional ride! Sure there is plenty of action within these pages. All while tugging at your heart strings with the current situation revolving around Shen. Losing a loved one and having the chance to bring them back is going to hit home with many readers I suspect. You do not want to miss out on this start of a new storyline for this series of TMNT. Go get your copy today!

Operation: Iron Coffin #3 delivers a thrilling, blood-soaked finale that balances outrageous action with genuine emotional weight. Kenny Porter brings Dracula’s conflict with his children to a satisfying close, while Tyrell Cannon and Shawn Lee give the issue relentless visual energy. Brutal, heartfelt, and wildly entertaining, this is a fitting conclusion to the series. This has been one of my favorite series of the year and is one of the most entertaining series on the shelves. If for whatever reason you missed this one, try and get the issues at your LCS this week. If you can’t find them, definitely pick up the trade when it drops, so you don’t miss out on one of the best series of the year!

“Operation: Iron Coffin” is an absolute tour de force from start to finish. If you ever feel down about yourself, read this to remind yourself you’re so much more. If someone or something like Dracula can redeem himself, then so can we.

Operation: Iron Coffin #2 keeps the momentum going with a bigger, bloodier, and more personal chapter for Dracula. Kenny Porter deepens the story without slowing down the action, while Tyrell Cannon’s artwork delivers the chaos, horror, and energy this concept demands. This series continues to be an absolute blast and remains an easy Pull List recommendation. Do not sleep on this series! Make sure you jump on this train now, as you don’t want to miss what happens next.

I don’t know how they’re doing it, but “Operation: Iron Coffin” is one of the best out this year. Kenny Porter manages to create a version of Dracula that feels relatable yet horrifying. His writing coupled with Cannon’s fantastic artwork create a truly amazing reading experience.
One of the best series in comics right now. The art is wild, creative, adventurous, and stunning. The story keeps drawing you back in issue after issue.
Marc Spector: Moon Knight #7 delivers an exhilarating ride with huge action, incredible artwork, and deadly stakes. It leaves you itching for the next issue.

The Smart Division is a fantastic science-fiction mystery that eerily could be more fact than fiction. Writer Zack Kaplan delivers a timely detective tale exploring the use of modern technology in solving crimes. However, it’s the juxtaposition of John Pearson’s elegant brush strokes that makes story rise above the rest. Kaplan and Pearson’s creativity knows no bounds and The Smart Division is proof of that.

I sat down with The Smart Division expecting a slick sci-fi detective story and walked away rattled about the world outside my window. That is the highest thing I can say about a comic right now. This is a perfect debut and one of the most relevant books on the stands, and I cannot wait to see where the case goes.

King Shazam and Superman throw down in a final fight for the ages! Arron leaves it all on table with the script. The art team never knows a ceiling in how far to raise the stakes. Highest possible recommendation.

Absolute Superman #21 feels like a true spectacle and lives up to the hype in every way as this arc comes to. a close. There is so much violence, emotion, and power packed into these pages that it may, in fact, be my favorite issue of the run yet.
Superman: The Stranger #1 returns to Clark Kent's roots, spinning a story that shows why Superman is such a timeless character.

The best Superman comic I’ve read in years!  A 1930s reinvention of the Man of Steel that returns Superman to his 1930s roots, but zigs and zags in ways you won’t expect, while keeping you on your toes. With a story that hooks you from the go and art and colours that leap off the page, this is a must-read mini-series.

Six of Us #1 turns a seemingly perfect 1990s sitcom cast into a web of secrets, resentment, and murder, with Tom King and Gabriel Hernández Walta delivering a compelling mystery that leaves everyone looking potentially guilty.

SIX OF US reminds us why this award winning creative team is so unstoppable. It's a human story about the importance of creating art, but the cost of it too. Six of Us #1 invites us to consider what true fulfillment looks like, and whether it has anything to do with success.
Black Tower: The Raven Conspiracy #1 is a compelling mix of magic and spy fiction, packed with haunting imagery and a unique mystery.

Black Tower: The Raven Conspiracy #1 proves that everything out of DC Vertigo should be jumped on immediately. This was a strong start to a comic series that has captured my attention from the first page and didn’t let go until the ending. I cannot recommend this comic enough!

The Smart Division #2 will inject a level of fear into the reader that they may not have thought an issue could do. This may be a story, but, Zack, John, and Hassan blur the lines of reality, posing ethical questions regarding AI and leaving us with an ending that sinks us deeper into the mystery.

The Smart Division #2 builds confidently on the series’ opening mystery with sharper tension, compelling character conflict, and an unsettling exploration of AI and corporate power. Zack Kaplan keeps the investigation unpredictable, while John J. Pearson delivers immersive artwork that strengthens the book’s noir atmosphere. This is a smart, suspenseful second issue that leaves the case more dangerous and more intriguing than ever. If this series isn’t already on your Pull List, reconsider that decision NOW.

Marshall makes his move but is it too late? That is the question haunting the road to Radiant Black #50. The writing balances out a reunion while attempting a daring rescue. Impressive images capture the moments to elevate the drama higher. Radiant Black continues to be the blueprint for modern superhero storytelling !
Radiant Black #44 kicks off a new story arc while testing the relationship at the core of the series. It also reminds us that the future isn't set in stone, whether you're a hero or a villain.

The Nice House by the Sea #12 delivers a riveting conclusion that puts Norah firmly in the driver's seat as two worlds hurtle toward destruction. James Tynion IV crafts a surprisingly accessible finale built around a tense series of conversations, while Álvaro Martínez Bueno and Jordie Bellaire make the impending apocalypse look breathtaking. The final pages focus more on setting up the next chapter than on providing complete closure, but there's no denying how effectively this issue brings its immediate conflict to a close.

One resident of the Houses attempts the unthinkable as the end of the world has arrived!! Tynion cuts deeply into the soul of the series with phenomenal writing. Bueno and Bellaire electrify as the art sweeps readers under its spell. An impressive journey into the soul of humanity.

The Seasons #12 is a dazzling penultimate issue that showcases Paul Azaceta's incredible imagination while Rick Remender explores the frustrations of being the youngest in a family that refuses to listen. Spring's struggle to be heard gives the fantastical adventure a surprisingly relatable emotional core, even as the story races through increasingly bizarre worlds. Some of the larger mysteries remain hard to grasp, but the sheer creativity makes this an exhilarating lead-in to the finale.

With each issue of this series I’ve waited for this team to let me down, I’ve been let down too many times in the past to expect greatness this far into a series. However, I’m done with that now. This team knows exactly what it is doing with this story, this art, this group of characters. This is exactly the team that Iron Man needed right now, a back to basics story with big goals for the future, an art team that knows how to handle a story this big, and this reader who is eagerly waiting for each issue!

Tony’s world is rocked again with the return of Happy Hogan! Williamson tears into the man behind the armor with superb writing. Carnero and the team construct excitement on each page. The legend of Tony Stark grows larger with every story told here!

This is but also isn’t your typical Spider-Man story. It carries some of the basic mainstream feel of a Spider-Man story and background. But with some twists along the way that get readers hooked after the introduction. The writing is intriguing, and the art is beyond eye-catching. Fans of Spider-Man will want to read this issue! If you’re just getting into Spider-Man, you will want to pick up this issue! There are so many Peter Parker details within this issue that new fans will gain an understanding of Spider-Man. Great debut issue for this brand new series! Get your copy today!

Midnight Spider-Man #1 sticks the landing as it reinvents the classic Marvel hero for the modern age, birthing him into a much darker and scarier world while keeping the core elements of what makes Peter Parker and Spider-Man tick. The engaging script and inventive art endlessly impress, but this is not a series for everyone.

I went into this not knowing what to expect, and was left with every expectation surpassed. Midnight X-Men #1 is dark; it’s brutal; it’s a home run. I cannot recommend this issue enough! Do yourself a favor and make sure it’s on your pull list!
It’s a dark, bloody, thought-provoking take on the X-Men that feels tailor-made for the Halloween season.

The Lanterns attempt a bold rescue while Guy Gardner gets some history from the Book of OA in another incredible issue. Hampton weaves many sub-plots while unloading solid action throughout. The art brings the energy with each and every panel. When you want the best of “Green Lantern” stories, this is what to read!

A lively bridge toward First Light, packed with Emotional Spectrum developments, Darkstar drama, and meaningful growth for Ellie Stewart. It sets up exciting possibilities but leaves some plot threads awaiting conclusion.

If “Midnight Fantastic Four” is anything to go by, this new universe is off to a truly great start. If you’re not already one, Percy will make a Fantastic Four fan out of you yet. The thrills and chills are building, so here’s to hoping the payoff will be fantastic.
The horror of the Marvel Midnight universe hits the Fantastic Four, as the creative team executes cosmic dread better than almost any other comic out there.

Legion of Super-Heroes #2 fully has my attention. This is a murder mystery mixed with a futuristic science fiction story that is so captivating. The team knows how to use plot and art to tell so much without ever feeling as though it is overstuffed.

R.J. Brande’s murder mystery grows into further chaos with another fantastic chapter. Williamson’s writing dives further into the lore of family dynamics. Sherman and Bonvillain construct amazing visuals at each turn. This is the definition of what L.O.S.H. should be!

This was a great standalone issue of the Black Cat series. Self-contained stories like these can often be thrown away as filler stories, but this creative team avoids that. They craft a story that helps develop Felicia in an emotional and meaningful way.

Black Cat #15 offers a solid standalone story that juggles a mountain of plot points while keeping the series' humorous tone. It might even make fans put on their fanciest clothes for the opera scenes.

Just when I think Barbara Gordon: Breakout can’t get any better, the sixth issue disproves that. By adding more characters, having more perspectives, and the plot constantly thickening, the creative team proves that they’re at the top of their game!

Overall, I think this may be the best issue of the book since the first couple, however it still falls into the trap of being extremely front- and-end loaded, and having a middle with pretty much no meat yet again, but with art that makes it outshine what came before.

Erica’s return to present time brings forth a much needed encounter behind heavy drama. Tynion IV opens deep wounds with incredible writing. Dell’edera and Muerto craft the intense exchanges with superb art. No one does slow burn drama better than SIKTC!

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Spawn '77 #2 delivers plenty of bloody action and a few genuinely striking visuals, especially when Spawn and the angel take center stage. Mark Spears handles the larger-than-life characters well, and the issue's final twist offers an intriguing reason to return. Unfortunately, the extra-sized page count doesn't feel entirely justified. With limited plot progression, extended action sequences, and…
pros: Excellent action choreography, particularly during the angel's brutal confrontation with police.
An intriguing cliffhanger introduces an unexpected twist.
cons: The nearly 60-page issue feels padded, with surprisingly little story progression.
Civilian character designs and flat backgrounds lack the visual polish of the supernatural characters.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Batman: Bad Seeds - Streets of Gotham #1 is a wonderfully human anthology that reminds us Gotham's greatest heroes don't always wear capes. Across six stories, an impressive lineup of creators explores how ordinary citizens respond when their city falls into chaos. The artwork is consistently strong, with each artist bringing a distinct personality to their corner of Gotham. It has plenty of heart…
pros: Six distinct stories offer compelling perspectives on everyday life during Gotham's latest crisis.
Excellent artwork throughout, particularly Jorge Fornes' gritty realism and Gretel Lusky's expressive character designs.
cons: Some stories are more memorable than others, with a few feeling relatively slight.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: A lively bridge toward First Light, packed with Emotional Spectrum developments, Darkstar drama, and meaningful growth for Ellie Stewart. It sets up exciting possibilities but leaves some plot threads awaiting conclusion.
pros: Intriguing Alpha Guardians, Book of Oa, and Emotional Entity developments.
Ellie, El, steps into her own as a capable Lantern.
Funny undercover scenes with Keli Quintela and Simon Baz.
cons: Several plot threads remain unresolved, as some story developments feel more like setup than payoff.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: An action-packed showcase of wonderful art that is held back by a disarmingly sloppy script and baffling character work.
pros: The art is very well done
The concept behind this issue was strong
cons: Everybody talks like they're subtweeting the writer's critics
Inconsistent and confusing characterization for our issue's lead character
Feels like it should have had it's place swapped with another issue
At worst, it feels like filler

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Teen Titans #2 delivers a propulsive sophomore issue that highlights the friction between Red Hood and his new team of Titans, and the challenges in their way. It also pushes the Teen Titans' mythos in bold new directions.
pros: Higgins's script highlights the friction between Red Hood and his new team of Titans.
Di Nicuolo doesn't skimp on action, emotion or general movement in his art, resulting in some eye grabbing pages.
Costa's colors makes the action – and the characters – pop.
A last minute twist that makes things personal.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Action Comics #1103 starts peeling back the layers of Lex Luthor's life, revealing the events that made him Superman's deadliest enemy. At times tragic and illuminating, it shows that even bad guys can be the focus of a good comic.
pros: The shift in focus to Lex Luthor works as fans will get to see more of his origins.
Waid spends a lot of time highlighting the differences between Luthor and Clark's upbringing.
More grounded than previous installments, but it works given who's the focus.
Delpeche's art remains as expressive and emotional as ever.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Nova: Return of the Rings #1 doubles as a triumphant return for Sam Alexander and a heartfelt celebration of his Hispanic heritage. With the special teasing that Sam and the Ten Rings will return in Josh Williamson's Iron Man, Nova's legacy looks set to keep burning brightly.
pros: A great opening essay that highlights why Sam Alexander's Hispanic heritage is important.
The "Shining Light" storyline is a great balance between superheroics and family matters.
The main story by Trujillo, Louriero, and Abdias brings Sam back into the superhero business with a great hook.
An ending that teases Nova's return in Iron Man, and the Marvel Universe, in general.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Wade Wilson: Deadpool #9 delivers the most entertaining "Big Guns" chapter yet, packing its pages with inventive action, brutal humor, and genuinely surprising twists. Benjamin Percy has a blast with the time gun concept, while Geoff Shaw's dynamic artwork makes every confrontation a treat. Black Hole finally gets some attention, and the bizarre final twist sets up an intriguing finale. It's a sha…
pros: Inventive use of the time gun leads to hilarious and unexpected moments.
Geoff Shaw delivers excellent action choreography and a wonderfully expressive Deadpool.
The Deadpool and Punisher confrontation is brief but delightfully vicious.
cons: Black Hole still feels underutilized despite being the crossover's central villain.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Black Cat #15 offers a solid standalone story that juggles a mountain of plot points while keeping the series' humorous tone. It might even make fans put on their fanciest clothes for the opera scenes.
pros: Wilson balances plenty of plot twists with outlandish humor and solid character moments.
Melnikov excels at drawing Felicia in a variety of situations and outfits.
Reber's colors perfectly capture the difference between New York at day and New York at night.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Midnight Spider-Man #1 puts a horrifying spin on Peter Parker's origins, complete with compelling yet gruesome art and a deconstruction of his iconic principles about great power and great responsibility.
pros: Johnson skillfully deconstructs Spidey's mantra of great power and great responsibility in a way that fits the Midnight Universe.
ScieTronc's artwork feels anime-inspired, and also ramps up the body horror.
Neeraj Menon's color work paints gore in vivid showers.
Plenty of characters from the Spider-Man mythos get reworked in surprising ways.
An ending that will leave you with chills.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Midnight X-Men #1 proves Jonathan Hickman still knows exactly how to make the X-Men feel dangerously unpredictable.
pros: Hickman immediately establishes an intriguing new status quo for the X-Men
The competing factions create plenty of mystery and potential conflict
Matteo Della Fonte’s detailed, realistic artwork makes the horror hit hard
cons: The larger world could use a little more definition
Action is relatively limited until the final third

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Midnight Fantastic Four #1 is a horrifying and menacing start to this darker take on Marvel's First Family, and serves as a great statement for the possibility of the Midnight line.
pros: Feels unique and fresh instead of just making our heroes into villains
Benjamin Percy's script does a great job of placing a sense of dread just below the surface of the story, so we know something bad will happen but we don't know…
Kev Walker's art is truly surprising in this, both in what he accomplishes gore wise and horror
Midnight Reed Richards might be one of the most sympathetic takes on the character I've ever read
Sets up a lot of interesting long term seeds for the title in the future
cons: Ben and Johnny don't have as much to do in this opening story as Reed and Sue
